nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$, let $A$ be a real number, and let $Y_n = X_n \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n| \le A\}}$ be the truncation of $X_n$ at $A$. If $\sum_n P(|X_n| > A) < \infty$, then for almost every $\omega$ we have $X_n(\omega) = Y_n(\omega)$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

nodes.summary: Let $Z_0, Z_1, \dots$ be independent integrable real random variables on a probability space with $E[Z_n] = 0$ for every $n$, and let $S_n = \sum_{k \le n} Z_k$. If there is a constant $R \ge 0$ with $E|S_n| \le R$ for every $n$, then $S_n$ converges almost surely to a finite limit.

nodes.summary: Let $(X_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence of independent measurable real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, and let $A > 0$. If $\sum_n \mu(\{\omega : |X_n(\omega)| > A\}) = \infty$, then there is no function $S : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ such that, for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, the partial sums $\sum_{i < n} X_i(\omega)$ converge to $S(\omega)$ as $n \to \infty$.

Then for every $A > 0$ the tail probabilities are summable:…

nodes.summary: For a uniformly bounded independent sequence whose partial sums converge almost surely, the variances are summable. Proved by symmetrization: the symmetrized sums are centered, so Paley–Zygmund gives a uniform lower bound on block-tail probabilities, contradicting convergence in measure unless the variances are summable.
nodes.title: Three-series necessity, second half of the variance step

nodes.summary: For a uniformly bounded independent sequence with summable variances whose partial sums converge almost surely, the partial sums of the means converge (to some limit). Proved by centering and applying the canonical centered-sum convergence theorem with an `L¹` bound from the total variance. The mean partial sums are the difference of the two convergent series at a single sample point.
nodes.title: Mean step of three-series necessity
